evidence: owner.lisp:3197-3202 `(:uncertain-reply (let ((octets (ignore-errors (apply #'fnn-core 'fn-owner-uncertain-reply-of render)))) (if (fnn-octet-list-p octets) (cons :close octets) :uncertain)))`. RENDER is nil for a member refused before its attempt (docstring at 3079-3080), so the apply calls fn-owner-uncertain-reply-of with no arguments.
fix: Check RENDER's shape explicitly (nil means :uncertain) and let any other condition propagate to fnn-owner-shared-action-locked, or at minimum log it with fnn-err before falling back to the bare close.
reviewer: The ignore-errors at 3197-3202 does swallow ACL2 or guard errors in fn-owner-uncertain-reply-of without logging them. The nil-RENDER part is refuted: fn-ocs-member-release (books/owner-commit-steps.lisp:342-347) names :uncertain-reply only when the member is renderable, otherwise :close, so apply is never called with nil. Heap exhaustion is also not swallowed, because storage-condition is not an error. What remains is a deliberate best-effort fallback: the client still gets an uncertain close. Its only defect is that the renderer fault is invisible, and it matters most on the stall-release path (3392-3407), where the service keeps running.
scenario: An ACL2 guard violation, a raw-ev-fncall throw or a heap-exhaustion storage-condition inside fn-owner-uncertain-reply-of, or an arity error from a nil RENDER, is silently turned into a plain close. The poster still gets 'uncertain', but the core fault that should stop the image (exit 4) never reaches the fault boundary and is not logged, so a broken uncertain-reply renderer goes unnoticed in every recovery event.
title: Uncertain-reply rendering swallows every error via ignore-errors, including core faults
